# OpenAI's $15B Raise and $1.25T Valuation + Daybreak Security Launch


By OpenTools Team


·


November 13, 2026


OpenAI raised $15 billion at a $1.25 trillion valuation — about half its original $30B target — while simultaneously launching Daybreak Red Team and Defense Factory, two agent‑based security products that automate penetration testing and vulnerability remediation at AI scale.


## $15 Billion, Half the Target


[OpenAI](https://opentools.ai/organizations/openai) has raised $15 billion at a $1.25 trillion valuation, CNBC's David Faber reported on Thursday, citing sources — about half the $30 billion the company originally sought from investors. The first close of $11 billion landed on November 6, with an additional $4 billion closing by November 12,[Dealroom](https://dealroom.co/news/172395-openai-raises-15b-at-a-1-25t-valuation-half-its-original-target-as-it-br/) and[Bloomberg](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-11-06/openai-completes-11-billion-portion-of-funding-at-1-25-trillion-value) reported.


The round was described as an "opportunistic raise to bridge the company to an initial public offering expected in 2027," per Dealroom. SoftBank and Abu Dhabi's MGX participated in the first close,[Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/ai/articles/openai-just-raised-11-billion-133842228.html) reported. CFO Sarah Friar said business grew 70% quarter-over-quarter, with revenue roughly split 50/50 between consumers and enterprise.


## The $1.25T Valuation: Growth, Burn, and an IPO on the Horizon


The new valuation is about 47% above[OpenAI](https://opentools.ai/organizations/openai) 's March 2026 round of $122 billion at $852 billion, but below the $1.4 trillion the company had initially targeted. The gap reflects cooling investor appetite amid a broader AI stock selloff,[the Wall Street Journal](https://www.wsj.com/tech/ai/openai-raises-less-than-half-of-30-billion-target-in-latest-round-91aecdc5) reported, citing "market jitters over the AI trade."


OpenAI's revenue is accelerating — roughly $10 billion in Q3, up nearly 50% from the previous quarter — but spending is growing faster. The company posted about $10.9 billion in operating losses for the quarter, driven by surging compute and data center costs,[Dealroom](https://dealroom.co/news/172395-openai-raises-15b-at-a-1-25t-valuation-half-its-original-target-as-it-br/) reported. OpenAI has received about $30 billion from[Nvidia](https://opentools.ai/organizations/nvidia) and about $65 billion from SoftBank to date. NVIDIA itself warned that frontier labs "are growing faster than what their balance sheets and credit profiles can support,"[Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/ai/articles/openai-just-raised-11-billion-133842228.html) noted.


The round lands one week before rival[Anthropic](https://opentools.ai/organizations/anthropic) lists on Nasdaq on November 19 with a price range of $70 to $78 per share and a target valuation of up to about $1.4 trillion, per Dealroom. A weak Anthropic debut could pressure both labs' valuations.


## Daybreak Red Team: Superhuman Pen-Testing at AI Scale


On the same day the funding news broke,[OpenAI](https://opentools.ai/organizations/openai) launched Daybreak Red Team and Daybreak Defense Factory, two agent-based security products under the Daybreak platform. Daybreak Red Team, now in early access, uses GPT-6 Cyber models to perform automated penetration testing of web applications,[The Register](https://www.theregister.com/security/2026/11/12/openai-launches-security-products-tells-orgs-theyre-doomed-if-they-dont-use-them/5309500) reported.


Nancy Wang, who leads cyber-applied AI at OpenAI, described Red Team as "superhuman pen-test at the scale of automated continuous scanning," with a fleet of agents using source code and application context to investigate and test attack paths, according to[The Register](https://www.theregister.com/security/2026/11/12/openai-launches-security-products-tells-orgs-theyre-doomed-if-they-dont-use-them/5309500) . The agents can also validate vulnerabilities from scanners, bug bounties, and disclosure reports, then test patches after they land.


OpenAI President Greg Brockman, in a Thursday keynote, framed the stakes in stark terms: "We're now at a point where companies will be secure only to the extent of the frontier model that they use to defend themselves and how well they utilize that,"[The Register](https://www.theregister.com/security/2026/11/12/openai-launches-security-products-tells-orgs-theyre-doomed-if-they-dont-use-them/5309500) reported.


## Defense Factory: Automating Find, Validate, and Fix


Defense Factory automates the full defensive loop — finding, validating, and fixing vulnerabilities at scale,[explainx.ai](https://explainx.ai/blog/openai-daybreak-red-team-defense-factory-launch-november-2026) detailed in a technical breakdown. The architecture ingests findings from existing tools including Snyk, Semgrep, Tenable,[GitHub](https://opentools.ai/organizations/github) code scanning, Dependabot, and Jira tickets, then dispatches Codex-class agents to reproduce issues, develop patches, and verify fixes in isolated environments.


"This way engineers get a merge-ready pull request with the patch and a test that shows that it works," Wang told[The Register](https://www.theregister.com/security/2026/11/12/openai-launches-security-products-tells-orgs-theyre-doomed-if-they-dont-use-them/5309500) . Humans remain the gate — engineers approve fixes before they merge into production. The system integrates with existing tools via MCPs, CLIs, and APIs rather than aiming to replace them,[explainx.ai](https://explainx.ai/blog/openai-daybreak-red-team-defense-factory-launch-november-2026) noted.


## The Builder Toolchain: Codex Security CLI and GitHub Integration


For developers, the most actionable piece is the open-source` @[openai](https://opentools.ai/organizations/openai) /codex-security` package — an Apache-licensed CLI and TypeScript SDK for integrating security scanning into CI pipelines and custom applications. A single command —` npx @openai/codex-security scan .` — runs automated security analysis against a codebase,[OpenAI's GitHub repository](https://github.com/openai/codex-security) details.


Builders can also trigger reviews directly from[GitHub](https://opentools.ai/organizations/github) pull requests by commenting` @codex security review` ,[explainx.ai](https://explainx.ai/blog/openai-daybreak-red-team-defense-factory-launch-november-2026) reported. The workflow covers repository scanning, backlog triage from SARIF exports or Jira tickets, and CI enforcement in GitHub Actions or GitLab. Codex Security has already scanned over 30 million commits across more than 30,000 codebases since launching in research preview in March, according to OpenAI's Daybreak page.


## What It Signals: Security as a Product Category for AI Labs


The dual announcement — a massive fundraise and a security product launch — is not a coincidence.[OpenAI](https://opentools.ai/organizations/openai) is signaling that security tooling has become a major product category, not just a research initiative. The company committed $1 billion to Daybreak for defending critical infrastructure including water, power, and banking systems, and the products now span both offensive (Red Team) and defensive (Defense Factory) workflows,[EdTech Innovation Hub](https://www.edtechinnovationhub.com/news/openai-commits-1-billion-to-help-defend-the-water-power-and-banking-systems-people-rely-on) reported.


The competitive landscape is shifting fast. CrowdStrike's Charlotte AI automates detection triage with 98% decision accuracy. Snyk's DeepCode AI generates vulnerability fixes in the IDE. But OpenAI's approach is different: rather than bolting AI onto an existing security platform, it is building security products from AI-first principles — agents that find, exploit, and fix vulnerabilities in a single loop. For builders, this means a new ecosystem of AI-powered AppSec tools is taking shape, and OpenAI is betting it can own the intelligence layer that powers them.


## The Bottom Line for Builders


[OpenAI](https://opentools.ai/organizations/openai) 's $15 billion raise at a $1.25 trillion valuation — half its original target — is a signal that even the industry's biggest name faces scrutiny as AI stocks sell off. But the real story for builders is the Daybreak launch, which turns vulnerability discovery and remediation into a productized, agent-driven workflow. The open-source Codex Security CLI gives developers a concrete on-ramp, and the Defense Factory architecture hooks into the tools teams already use. The message from OpenAI is clear: security is no longer a feature — it is a platform play, and the AI models that power it are becoming as important as the code they protect.
